nodes.label: One Data Model per Real-World Entity
nodes.norm_label: one data model per real-world entity
nodes.rationale: Customer, address, payment method, product, order and invoice each exist once; document types are views over the same records rather than parallel copies that drift.

nodes.label: Order-to-Invoice Metadata Bridge
nodes.rationale: A storefront order carries customer, line items, amount and payment state into the finance spine using the same invoice entity shape as a bespoke job, so revenue is reconciled identically.

nodes.label: Pickup as a First-Class Checkout Option
nodes.norm_label: pickup as a first-class checkout option
nodes.rationale: The customer selects a location and the order records it, rather than pretending collection is shipping to a fixed address.

nodes.label: Bank Transaction Reconciliation
nodes.rationale: Every transaction is matched to a specific document or explicitly written off by a person; an unmatched difference is a real signal, not rounding noise.

nodes.label: Derived Monthly Statistics
nodes.rationale: The month is computed from expense and income records rather than accumulated into a second table, so it cannot drift from its inputs and closing a month is not an operation.

nodes.label: Expense Capture and Approval Workflow
nodes.rationale: An approval step makes expense data trustworthy enough to reconcile and stops one person's mis-typing becoming a settled fact.

nodes.label: Two-Way Google Sheets Bridge
nodes.rationale: Application-owned record identity survives row sorting, and an explicit column range contract prevents overwriting spreadsheet formulas; saves built on stale external edits are rejected.

nodes.label: Deposit Percentage from Quotation
nodes.rationale: A deposit percentage recorded once in the document the client agreed to produces the first instalment automatically, rather than being retyped into the invoice.

nodes.label: Quotation Line Items with Derived Totals
nodes.norm_label: quotation line items with derived totals
nodes.rationale: The total is derived from description/quantity/rate lines rather than typed in, so the PDF, dashboard and email all read the same value and a third revision cannot carry stale arithmetic.

nodes.label: Quotation Revision History
nodes.rationale: Revisions are a property of the quotation rather than separate documents, because scope changes are normal and disputes about what was quoted are expensive.

nodes.label: Quotation-to-Invoice Conversion
nodes.rationale: Acceptance converts rather than copies because line items, customer, company profile and address are references to one source of truth; this stops quotation and invoice drifting apart.

nodes.label: Split-Payment Instalments
nodes.rationale: An invoice settles across several instalments with their own status so deposit, milestones and balance do not require duplicate invoices or demanding the full amount up front.

nodes.label: Business Core Monolith
nodes.rationale: Expenses, invoices, quotations and company profiles are read and written together, so splitting them would put a network hop and a failure mode inside a single business fact.

nodes.rationale: Directory split cmd/ + internal/domain + internal/application + internal/infrastructure with repository ports is why domain-driven design, layered and hexagonal patterns are all reported; the memory and filesystem repositories are interchangeable adapters behind one port.

nodes.label: G-NAF API Key System
nodes.rationale: Keys are stored as fast cryptographic hashes rather than Argon2/bcrypt because they are high-entropy random values and a slow KDF would inflate every autocomplete request; controls include domain binding, per-key rate limits, expiry and Turnstile at registration.

nodes.label: Cloudflare Tunnel Container Deployment
nodes.rationale: Cloudflare fronts a tunnel into the API container, which reaches PostgreSQL on the internal Docker network with a persistent volume, so the database is never publicly exposed.

nodes.label: p95 < 50 ms Uncached Autocomplete Benchmark
nodes.rationale: 1,000 mixed query shapes on full data measured p50 ~7 ms / p95 ~26 ms / p99 ~28 ms with the suggestion cache disabled, on an M5 Pro with Dockerised PostgreSQL — an environment measurement, not an infrastructure guarantee.

nodes.label: Nine Parallel State/Territory Workers
nodes.rationale: One worker per state dataset makes ingestion concurrent; combined with COPY the whole load prepares in roughly 9–10 minutes on development hardware.

nodes.label: Repeatable Release Refresh
nodes.rationale: Because Geoscape republishes during the year, the quarterly refresh is the same parameterised code path as the initial load.

nodes.label: Query Classifier Intent
nodes.rationale: Normalisation (trim, lowercase, collapse whitespace, strip punctuation) makes '12 main st sydney' and 'Main St. Sydney NSW' comparable before intent is derived.

nodes.label: Fixed Autocomplete Query Pipeline
nodes.rationale: API key auth → parser → LRU cache → classifier → tier router, with exactly one PostgreSQL strategy chosen before the database is touched.

nodes.label: Search Tier Router
nodes.rationale: Maps intent to B-tree prefix, composite B-tree, trigram GIN or correction-then-prefix, because the three query shapes have entirely different selectivity and index behaviour.

nodes.label: Typo Correction into Indexed Path
nodes.rationale: Corrected input is routed back to fast indexed paths rather than sending every imperfect query to a fuzzy scan; trigram GIN remains the fallback only when no correction yields a matchable prefix.

nodes.label: COPY FROM STDIN Streaming Load
nodes.rationale: Streaming rows instead of building huge JS arrays keeps the working set a bounded stream across a ~16 million address load.

nodes.label: Staging Tables then Materialized Search View
nodes.norm_label: staging tables then materialized search view
nodes.rationale: Keeping raw relational rows intact lets denormalisation be re-run without re-reading PSV files, and rebuilding indexes on a prepared view is fast whereas re-joining normalised tables per keystroke is not.

nodes.label: PostgreSQL-Only Search Decision
nodes.rationale: Chose PostgreSQL over Elasticsearch/OpenSearch/Redis; the multi-tier router is what makes that viable by concentrating each query shape onto the index built for it.

nodes.label: Shared Authentication Across Storefront, CMS and Medusa
nodes.norm_label: shared authentication across storefront, cms and medusa
nodes.rationale: Credentials and user information are coordinated between storefront, Payload CMS and Medusa so the user experience stays consistent instead of fragmenting into separate logins.

nodes.label: Server-Side Role-Based Access Control
nodes.rationale: Roles are checked where the data is served, not by hiding UI buttons, so a crafted request cannot reach a capability the role lacks.

nodes.label: Single Identity Authority
nodes.rationale: Authentication lives only in the API server; the web app and commerce backend delegate to it, avoiding two drifting implementations of password rules, session expiry and role checks.

nodes.label: Read-Only Agent Tool Set
nodes.rationale: search_knowledge, list_owned_projects, coding_stats, coding_history, site_content and services cannot construct SQL, touch the filesystem or run a command, so a hallucinated call has no dangerous action available.

nodes.label: CMS Hardening Defaults
nodes.rationale: GraphQL disabled outright, relationship depth capped at five, public user creation disabled, five-failure login lockout for ten minutes, S3-compatible media adapter when configured.

nodes.label: Three-Axis Tool Bounds
nodes.rationale: Fixed Zod schema per tool, per-call timeout, and result truncation at 600 chars (6,000 with retrieval project ids, SSE summary capped at 400) — the contract is expected to stay concise rather than the cap being raised.

nodes.label: Bounded Chat Diagnostics
nodes.rationale: Optional restricted webhook records query, labels, retrieval candidates and usage asynchronously, never cookies, credentials, signed tokens, contact contents or raw exceptions — a record stops being trustworthy the moment it becomes an unrestricted sink.

nodes.label: Branch Preview Build Limitation
nodes.rationale: Previews cannot build because Payload validates production-critical env during type generation; making the vars optional would turn a correct build failure into an incorrect runtime deployment, so the fix belongs in deployment config.

nodes.label: Payload serverURL as Security Property
nodes.rationale: Payload derives cookie and CORS behaviour from serverURL, so loopback, HTTP-only production or unparseable values are refused at boot — booting quietly with the wrong cookie policy is the worse outcome.

nodes.label: PUBLIC_SITE_URL as Build-Time Configuration
nodes.rationale: The origin is baked into canonical URLs, Open Graph, sitemap, robots and security.txt; getting it wrong looks perfect while search engines are pointed elsewhere, so it is validated as production-critical.

nodes.label: Evidence Wrapper as Injection Boundary
nodes.rationale: Retrieval output, tool results, history and visitor input are wrapped as untrusted data because a portfolio necessarily carries Markdown, code and copied docs containing instruction-like sentences.

nodes.label: Layered Abuse Controls
nodes.rationale: Validation, rate limiting, Turnstile, semantic moderation, tool restrictions and timeouts each cover a failure the others cannot; Zod runs both at the HTTP boundary and again in the tool runner.

nodes.label: Separate Chat/Contact Rate Buckets
nodes.rationale: Screening consumes the contact budget because sharing the chat bucket made the most expensive operation the cheapest to drive; the window is Postgres-backed so limits survive restarts and hold across instances.

nodes.label: Per-Workflow Turnstile Actions
nodes.rationale: Chat, screening and final send use distinct action types so a token cannot be replayed across workflows; screening is gated ahead of the work because it costs two model calls and leaving it on the send would expose the expensive path without a verified human.

nodes.label: Business as Recommended Default Package
nodes.rationale: A typical small-business site needs an editable blog and a CMS, which Starter deliberately omits, so Business is the usual choice.

nodes.label: No CMS in Starter, by Design
nodes.norm_label: no cms in starter, by design
nodes.rationale: Starter is deliberately a five-page presence without content management; any blog, editable CMS, email integration or analytics moves the project to Business.

nodes.label: Malware Scanning and Safe Response Headers
nodes.norm_label: malware scanning and safe response headers

nodes.label: Pending-then-Attached Upload Lifecycle
nodes.rationale: Splitting upload into pending and attached states keeps abandoned uploads identifiable and lets storage/metadata failures be reconciled by a retry or cleanup process.

nodes.label: Private Bucket with Short-Lived Signed URLs
nodes.norm_label: private bucket with short-lived signed urls
nodes.rationale: Object storage stays private and access is mediated by the application or short-lived signed URLs, so guessing an object URL cannot expose another user's receipt.

nodes.label: Unpredictable Object Keys
nodes.rationale: Generating keys instead of using the original filename prevents enumeration and path-injection through user-controlled names.

nodes.label: Untrusted Upload Boundary
nodes.rationale: Every uploaded file is untrusted input; validation must inspect actual contents rather than the client-supplied MIME type.

nodes.label: Content-Fingerprint PDF Cache
nodes.rationale: A fingerprint over line items, totals, numbering, company details, address and payment profiles decides whether to reuse the stored object; guarding the upload as well as the render keeps the cache from being pointless.

nodes.label: Token-Scoped Public Share Links
nodes.rationale: A link authorises exactly one document, so there is no session to steal and no privilege to escalate; leakage damage is bounded by that document.

nodes.label: Decision Model (Perplexity Decider via OpenRouter Decisions API)
nodes.norm_label: decision model (perplexity decider via openrouter decisions api)
nodes.rationale: Sole owner of scope, safety and source selection (use/skip/uncertain), plus post-retrieval relevance judgement and contact/form screening; never writes visitor-facing text.

nodes.label: Four-Step Planner/Responder Loop
nodes.rationale: Each step re-decides against the previous results, so a request needing one fact to choose the next fetch neither pre-pays for both retrievals nor guesses wrong.

nodes.label: Responder Model
nodes.rationale: Owns language and presentation only (third-person Zita about itself, first-person Nelson about his work); no source authority and no mid-answer tool requests.

nodes.label: Tool Argument Planner
nodes.rationale: May argue only for tool names the decision model approved and gets one repair without changing tool name or id — authority split from arguments stops invented capability.

nodes.label: Relevance Gate at 0.60
nodes.rationale: Runs on the top 3 reranked candidates and asks whether the document is direct support, not merely related; a failure leaves it as a reranker fallback and marks the result degraded rather than discarding evidence.

nodes.label: Retrieval View Boundary
nodes.rationale: The browser receives citation titles and URLs with a generic degraded indicator, never chunk text or provider scores; what the model sees and what the visitor sees are deliberately different sets.

nodes.label: Decision/Planner/Responder Role Split
nodes.rationale: Classification, argument construction and prose generation are different problems; one collapsing prompt is easier to write but lets a model asked to pick a source quietly pick none.

nodes.label: Uncertain Delegates to Deterministic Routing
nodes.rationale: 'uncertain' is the only label that may fall back to routing; use/skip stay authoritative, so the model can say it does not know without the system degenerating to 'search everything'.

nodes.label: Retrieval After Moderation
nodes.rationale: Scope and safety screening precedes embedding work, so a rejected request never reaches the expensive part of the turn.

nodes.label: Moderation Calibration Trade-off
nodes.rationale: High-risk uncertainty fails closed, yet thresholds are tuned to avoid rejecting legitimate enquiries — both directions are optimised, so it is calibration work rather than configuration.

nodes.label: Import Cutoff Is Data, Not Code
nodes.norm_label: import cutoff is data, not code

nodes.label: indexKnowledgeSource Job
nodes.rationale: Publishing hooks enqueue indexing through Payload's job system (chunk, embed, write), deletion triggers cleanup, and retries use exponential backoff so a transient embedding failure does not drop a source.

nodes.label: Semantic Reranker
nodes.rationale: Reads query and candidate together and only reorders the capped 10 — it fixes ordering, not recall.

nodes.label: Versioned Idempotent Seed Snapshot
nodes.rationale: Non-idempotent seeding makes the practical response to a corpus fix a manual database edit that no test covers — idempotence is what lets a live environment be re-seeded.

nodes.label: Source Identity type:sourceId
nodes.rationale: No implicit join exists across the two databases, so identity is carried deliberately at the source level — re-chunking a document replaces its chunks and touches nothing else.

nodes.label: Two-Database Split
nodes.rationale: DATABASE_URL holds CMS/application data and KNOWLEDGE_DATABASE_URL holds embeddings, vector index, GitHub knowledge and the WakaTime warehouse; the reason is operational — retrieval can be reindexed or scaled, and a runaway analytics query cannot lock editorial tables.

nodes.label: Independently Updated Corpus Sources
nodes.rationale: Posts, GitHub reports, interviews, service docs and WakaTime data update independently and may be current while disagreeing, so count-style questions cannot be answered from retrieval.

nodes.label: Embedding Workload Split
nodes.rationale: Bulk indexing uses a local llama-server with Qwen3-Embedding-0.6B (no per-document cloud cost, no provider dependency during an index run) while online queries may use SiliconFlow for latency; both write 1024-dim vectors to one HNSW cosine index.

nodes.label: RAG Optional behind KNOWLEDGE_RAG_ENABLED
nodes.rationale: Disabled means no model file, no embedding sidecar, no pgvector query, and the portfolio never depends on AI infrastructure being up; a near-timeout offline message in local dev is the signature of an unreachable sidecar, not a slow model.

nodes.label: Staged Retrieval with Per-Stage Budget
nodes.rationale: Embed → pgvector top 10 → rerank → relevance gate → context, because vector distance identifies topical proximity, not an answer to the question.

nodes.label: Single-Purpose Python Micro-services
nodes.rationale: NLP, alignment, audio retrieval, enrichment, speech synthesis and image generation each earn separation by being slow, bursty or independently failing, so a model that fails to load does not take down search.

nodes.label: Signed Internal Calls
nodes.rationale: Signing covers compromise inside the boundary; making the services unreachable covers everything else.

nodes.label: Unpublished Micro-services
nodes.rationale: No exposed port and no edge-proxy route: reachable only over the private network from the API server.

nodes.label: Micro-service Contract Snapshot Gate
nodes.rationale: A signature verifies the caller, not the shape, so internal-shape drift needs its own committed-snapshot gate.

nodes.label: OpenAPI and Typed-Client Drift Check
nodes.rationale: Generated output is committed precisely so a contract change without regeneration yields a diff; regenerating per build would make the check vacuous.

nodes.label: Layered Quality Gates
nodes.rationale: Silent degradation (plausible-but-off alignment, missing column, removed field) never throws, so gates run where a violation can be caught: CI for code, startup for schema, content build for provenance.

nodes.label: Four-Layer API Server
nodes.rationale: Domain knows nothing about frameworks, application orchestrates, infrastructure implements ports, interface is the only HTTP layer — dependencies point inward so business rules are testable without a database or request.

nodes.label: Single Browser-Facing API Rule
nodes.rationale: Direct browser-to-micro-service calls would publish an internal service, put credentials in browser code, and let a compromised session drive expensive model work — so the API server answers everything and fans out invisibly.

nodes.label: Thin Learner Web App
nodes.rationale: Content is owned by the API server with one copy of truth and one seeding point; the web app owns only per-session state, so either side can be replaced without touching the other.

nodes.label: Strapi env validation layer
nodes.rationale: Splits Server/Client/Shared variables and caches the parsed env, so a missing secret fails at boot rather than at first request and the client bundle only receives public keys.

nodes.label: lst97.dev rebuild on TanStack Start with Strapi
nodes.norm_label: lst97.dev rebuild on tanstack start with strapi
nodes.rationale: The rework drops Next.js for TanStack Start + Router with Drizzle/Postgres, TanStack Query and Paraglide i18n, and externalises CMS content to a Strapi client; the /demo routes (server funcs, SSR SPA mode, api-request) show the migration was validated feature-by-feature against the old site.

nodes.label: Adapter/Facade Incremental Refactor
nodes.rationale: An adapter keeps the public API stable while internals move, avoiding a big-bang rewrite that forces every caller to change at once.

nodes.label: Behavioural Baseline Tests Before Refactor
nodes.rationale: Tests written against existing behaviour pin what users depend on, so a refactor can change structure without changing observable behaviour.

nodes.label: Shared Domain Module Extraction
nodes.rationale: Duplication is removed by extracting the real shared domain behaviour, not by scattering generic helpers.

nodes.label: Avoid Premature Abstraction
nodes.rationale: A full SaaS platform from day one would have been premature over-engineering; the lesson is to separate customer-specific behaviour without building abstractions before evidence requires them.

nodes.label: Generic Invoicing and Quotation Domain
nodes.rationale: Company profiles, customers, quotations, invoices, line items and document generation are not Best Maker-specific; separating that domain from customer-specific presentation and rules would have made multi-tenancy far cheaper.

nodes.norm_label: generated api types via hey api

nodes.label: Expand-and-Contract Migration
nodes.rationale: Add new schema, deploy code supporting both, migrate data, switch consumers, then drop the old schema in a later release — never rename or delete in one step.

nodes.label: Static Typing on Top of JavaScript
nodes.norm_label: static typing on top of javascript
nodes.rationale: Server response types can be shared with the frontend and regenerated when the server changes, removing manual tracking of every frontend type.

nodes.label: React and Next.js Ecosystem Choice
nodes.rationale: Mature ecosystem, documentation and full-stack features (routing, SSR, server components, API handling) reduce infrastructure that must be built by hand.

nodes.label: TypeScript Early Error Detection
nodes.rationale: Problems that would surface only at runtime in JavaScript are caught during development; defined types also give AI-assisted development context about how parts of the system interact.

nodes.label: Committed Generated API Client
nodes.rationale: Committing the generated client is what makes the drift check meaningful; regenerating fresh each build would let a contract change ship silently.

nodes.label: Contract-First Route Schemas
nodes.rationale: The OpenAPI document is derived from the code serving requests, so there is no window where documented and real APIs disagree.

nodes.label: Alignment Provenance and Quality Evidence
nodes.rationale: A half-second-shifted alignment passes every structural check; only a stored quality score plus reviewable provenance distinguishes it from a correct one.

nodes.label: Derived Sentence Annotation
nodes.rationale: Annotation is a lookup into the lexical corpus, not hand-authoring, so adding a sentence needs no annotation work and cannot disagree with the dictionary entry.

nodes.label: Karaoke Timing View
nodes.rationale: Text, readings and translation stay synchronised with audio; karaoke adds the stored per-word timing interval and reads the same lines and links, so it is not a separate content model.

nodes.label: Lyric-to-Dictionary Bidirectional Link
nodes.rationale: Line tokens link to entries and entries show real corpus lines, so context leads to the dictionary and the dictionary is anchored in real usage instead of invented examples.

nodes.label: Practice Loop with XP
nodes.rationale: Flashcards and speaking challenges grade an attempt and award XP/levels/streaks; progress events are idempotent per attempt and rewards attach to the same vocabulary being studied so the loop points at content, not the score.

nodes.label: Layered Sentence Page
nodes.rationale: Readings/POS, scene illustration, prepared translation and related sentences each answer a question the others cannot; request-time translation of pedagogical content is a translation nobody reviewed.

nodes.label: Vocabulary Plans
nodes.rationale: Themed groupings that build toward a task, with every word already a real corpus entry so a learner never has to leave the plan to look something up.

nodes.label: Single Lexical Corpus Spine
nodes.rationale: Meaning lives in context, so sentences, expressions, lyrics and karaoke are projections of one corpus rather than separate content sets.

nodes.label: Persisted Crawl Scheduler
nodes.rationale: node-cron with env-configurable schedule creates scheduled crawls and crawl jobs carrying their own result and session records, making a multi-day refresh queryable rather than log-only.

nodes.label: Database-backed Dead Letter Queue
nodes.rationale: Persists facility, district, date, error type, status, attempt count, failure times, next retry and crawl job, turning 'what is failing' into a query and preserving visibility logs would lose.

nodes.label: Jittered Exponential Backoff
nodes.rationale: Jitter prevents all failed tasks retrying at the same instant while backoff reduces pressure on an unhealthy upstream.

nodes.label: Crawl Instead of Browser Proxy
nodes.rationale: Six concrete reasons: external availability dependency, LCSD-dependent latency, duplicate upstream requests, no historical state, harder large-result filtering, and an external outage becoming an application outage.

nodes.label: p-queue Concurrency Bound
nodes.rationale: Limited concurrency over upstream requests because LCSD is a dependency the project does not control; protecting it also protects the application.

nodes.label: Circuit Breaker
nodes.rationale: CLOSED/OPEN/HALF-OPEN stops upstream requests at a failure threshold and probes after cooldown, because retrying during a full outage wastes resources and cascades failure.

nodes.label: Failure Classification Before Retry
nodes.rationale: Timeouts, connection failures, 5xx and parse failures are retryable; 4xx and 404 are usually permanent, because retrying a rejected request adds load without changing the outcome.

nodes.label: Zod Boundary Normalisation into Domain Entities
nodes.norm_label: zod boundary normalisation into domain entities
nodes.rationale: Every external response is validated then normalised into District/Facility/FacilityType/Session/CrawlJob, so invalid upstream data cannot corrupt internal state and the frontend never learns SmartPLAY's shape.

nodes.label: CantoLyr lexicon and lyric workbench
nodes.rationale: Lexicon lookup (AI, pronunciation, rhyme) and lyric search/generation share one React context layer so filters, result summaries and AI requests stay consistent across modes.

nodes.label: Payload CMS integration in canto-101-server
nodes.rationale: Payload embedded in a Next.js app gives an admin UI plus REST/GraphQL routes over Postgres, so Cantonese learning content is edited in one place instead of hand-written data files.

nodes.rationale: Neuron state is initialised and updated to bias move selection; the ANN is an alternative solver to backtracking and Warnsdorff rather than a dependency of them.

nodes.label: Backtracking Algorithm (BT class)
nodes.rationale: Declared as the backtracking-algorithm topic and materialised as the BT class; the exhaustive search the other strategies are compared against.

nodes.label: Warnsdorff Heuristic (Warnsdorff class)
nodes.rationale: Declared as a GitHub topic and as a class in algorithm.py: a move-ordering heuristic used to make the backtracking search tractable.

nodes.label: Backward-Compatible Inter-Service Contracts
nodes.rationale: Because frontend, API, database and workers deploy separately, each version must tolerate the immediately previous and next version instead of assuming atomic rollout.

nodes.label: Avoid Premature Sharding
nodes.rationale: Connection pooling, query optimisation, caching, read replicas and vertical scaling come before partitioning, because distributed databases carry large operational cost.

nodes.label: Measure the Bottleneck First
nodes.rationale: Scale the component that measurement proves to be the bottleneck rather than redesigning the whole system prematurely.

nodes.label: On-Demand PDF Rendering
nodes.rationale: Eager rendering on every save would render documents nobody asked for; rendering when a document is sent, shared or opened matches actual demand.

nodes.label: Outbox Queued Rendering
nodes.rationale: Rendering takes tens of seconds in a headless browser, so it is enqueued as an outbox intent and drained by a worker; a leaked browser kills a worker, not the dashboard.

nodes.label: Outbox Pattern
nodes.rationale: A user-facing request appends the intent and returns; a separate worker drains it, so slow side effects stay outside the latency budget and bursts do not become concurrent browser instances.

nodes.label: Split Out Slow, Bursty or Independently Failing Work
nodes.norm_label: split out slow, bursty or independently failing work
nodes.rationale: The service-extraction rule is about failure characteristics, not org chart: work gets its own process only if it is slow, bursty, or fails independently.

nodes.label: Signed and Time-Stamped Internal Requests
nodes.rationale: Unpublished services are reachable only from the API server; the signature proves caller identity and the timestamp bounds replay of a captured request.

nodes.label: Alignment Validation and Quality Score
nodes.rationale: Ordering, duration bounds, coverage, overlap and total span are checked before storage, and low-confidence results surface for review because plausible-but-wrong karaoke teaches the wrong timing.

nodes.label: Song Audio Download Micro-Service
nodes.rationale: Neither the browser nor the API server fetches third-party media directly, so the blast radius of touching an external media source is exactly one service.

nodes.label: Raw Timings Kept Auditable
nodes.rationale: Clamping or interpolating produces a result that looks correct but was never performed; corrections are review decisions, and provenance records which audio, preparation and validation produced each timing.

nodes.label: Vocals Isolation
nodes.rationale: Dense percussive instrumentation defeats alignment, so the vocal is isolated; doing it in the pipeline keeps every imported song prepared identically instead of mixing hand- and machine-prepared audio.

nodes.label: Word-to-Time Alignment Micro-Service
nodes.rationale: Alignment produces the interval each word is sung; it runs in its own service because it is slow and needs model weights the product server should not host, called over a signed internal request.

nodes.label: Credit Netting
nodes.rationale: Cross-debts net before payment is decided, and the UI exposes subtotal, auto-applied credit, previously applied credit, net amount and remaining balance so the history is explainable.

nodes.label: Debt Coverage Traceability
nodes.rationale: A settlement is associated with the expense records it resolves, so a partial payment can report which expenses remain outstanding instead of only a single amount.

nodes.label: Member Splitting and Net Balances
nodes.rationale: A payer's contribution minus their own share yields a net balance; negative owes, positive is owed, aggregated across transactions.

nodes.label: Date-Specific Historical Exchange Rate
nodes.rationale: Today's rate for a weeks-old expense distorts settlement, so lookup is by transaction date with fallback to the most recent earlier daily rate stored in SQLite (both directions) and historical rows are never revalued.

nodes.label: Deterministic Settlement Tests
nodes.rationale: A financial regression silently produces the wrong amount of money, the one failure mode a group ledger cannot afford, so settlement logic is tested without the UI.

nodes.label: Settlements Separate from Debts
nodes.rationale: Money owed and money paid are different facts; recording payments as their own settlement transactions is what allows outstanding, historical, settled, partial and credit-applied totals.

nodes.label: Exact then Greedy Debt Subset Selection
nodes.norm_label: exact then greedy debt subset selection
nodes.rationale: Small candidate sets get exact combinatorial search ordered by fewer records, lower over-coverage, fewer indirect records and deterministic ties; large sets switch to greedy plus local improvement so cost stays bounded.

nodes.rationale: Repairs an existing AI-generated project rather than building a new site; quoted individually after code review because repair scope varies widely.

nodes.label: Chat agent loop
nodes.rationale: Drives up to four steps, keeps per-turn state, guards tool execution and event sequencing; catalogue-plus-details is intentionally sequential (catalogue first, then a fresh detail decision).

nodes.label: Chat source boundaries (inventory vs knowledge vs site_content vs services)
nodes.norm_label: chat source boundaries (inventory vs knowledge vs site_content vs services)
nodes.rationale: Each source answers only its own question class: list_owned_projects for canonical inventory/counts, search_knowledge for owner facts and interview answers, site_content for published Payload state, coding_stats/coding_history for WakaTime, services for the commercial offer (fixed RAG query, no steering). Multiple sources only when the latest request needs each.

nodes.label: Signed chat contact workflow state machine
nodes.norm_label: signed chat contact workflow state machine
nodes.rationale: Contact mode is a signed explicit state (template_selection, filling, review, delivered) that is screened and locked, cannot fall through to normal chat, clears prior chat history on confirmation, and binds review approval with an HMAC proof plus a Postgres one-time claim before SMTP.

nodes.label: Decision model (perplexity/pplx-decider-v1.2)
nodes.rationale: System One compatible decider on OpenRouter's Decisions API; it classifies scope and safety and labels each source use/skip/uncertain, but never writes the answer or prepares tool arguments. Explicit use/skip is authoritative; only literal 'uncertain' may fall back to deterministic routing.

nodes.label: OpenRouter planner (tool-argument preparation)
nodes.rationale: Receives only decision-approved tool names; may repair one rejected call but cannot reselect sources or write the final answer.

nodes.label: OpenRouter responder (answer writing)
nodes.rationale: Writes the user-facing answer from supplied evidence and tool results; its persona rules live only in the responder prompt, not in decision or planner prompts.

nodes.label: Zita (on-site portfolio assistant)
nodes.rationale: Nelson-representative persona: first person for Nelson's verified work, accounts and commercial offer, third person for questions about the assistant itself.

nodes.label: RAG read path (query → embed → search → rerank → gate → evidence)
nodes.norm_label: rag read path (query → embed → search → rerank → gate → evidence)
nodes.rationale: Message → query-resolution → query embedding → exact pgvector search (30 candidates) → diversity trim (≤10) → SiliconFlow rerank → dedupe/top-3 → per-document relevance gate → evidence budget → untrusted evidence block → citations. RetrieveKnowledge.execute is the only entry the chat calls; RAG is opt-in and retrieval failure degrades to knowledgeUnavailable instead of blocking a reply.

nodes.label: Per-document relevance gate
nodes.rationale: Decides direct support per document at 0.60 thresholds; sends one document per request because the decider is grouping-sensitive.

nodes.label: Decision-model decision surface
nodes.rationale: Four ModerationClassifier methods each make exactly one systemOne({state, questions}) call through a fetch client (5s timeout, 3 attempts, jittered 250ms base, Retry-After honoured up to 2s); non-transient failures and invalid responses are never retried, and any throw becomes { unavailable: true } so callers fail closed.

nodes.label: AI-assisted code failure modes
nodes.rationale: AI assistance produces convincing-looking but structurally unsound code: prototype that only runs on the generating machine, unfinished authentication, assumed rather than declared env vars, and unreviewed security defaults; generated-code cleanup is part of the service because duplication, dead branches and hardcoded values make later maintenance expensive.

nodes.label: Vercel BotID as additive gate
nodes.rationale: BotID is layered over Turnstile and the rate limit, not a replacement: a failed check degrades to 'not a bot' and logs bot.unavailable, so a BotID outage cannot take chat offline; the client protected-path list and server checks must stay in agreement.

nodes.label: Chat diagnostics redaction policy
nodes.rationale: Request-scoped observer callbacks send a redacted bounded turn record to a restricted Discord channel; contact message text and form values never reach app logs or Discord, credentials/tokens/raw exceptions never enter prompts or SSE, and usage is reported only when providers report it.

nodes.label: Tool output truncation budget (600/6,000 chars, 400 SSE)
nodes.norm_label: tool output truncation budget (600/6,000 chars, 400 sse)
nodes.rationale: agent-loop.ts slices results to 600 chars (6,000 when retrieval.projectSourceIds is present) and the SSE tool_result summary to 400; an over-budget op silently loses its tail to the model while still showing in the DOM, so absolute URLs belong in retrieval.citations and the cap must not be raised to fit an op.

nodes.label: Separate Turnstile actions (chat_message / contact / contact_screening)
nodes.rationale: Screening is gated ahead of the work, not only at send: submit_form spends two model calls, so it needs its own contact_screening token and the 5/hour contact bucket; separate actions prevent replaying a chat-message or send token to screen a form. Tokens are single-use control data and never enter prompts, history, signed context or diagnostics.

nodes.label: Exact vector scan invariant
nodes.rationale: SET LOCAL enable_indexscan = off forces a sequential scan so ORDER BY embedding <=> cannot take an approximate HNSW walk that misses the true nearest chunk; no reranker or gate can recover a chunk that never entered the pool. Single-digit milliseconds at this corpus size; revisit above roughly 10^4–10^5 chunks with high hnsw.ef_search.

nodes.label: Private evidence is retrievable and labelled
nodes.norm_label: private evidence is retrievable and labelled
nodes.rationale: search returns every row with is_public; retrieval drops non-http(s) URLs but serves private chunks stamped isPublic:false and labelled 'private repository (sanitized summary; safe to summarize for the user)'. Public-only SQL filtering is explicitly forbidden because it would silently drop them.

nodes.label: Project deep-dive documents
nodes.rationale: One hand-authored document per topic for gnaf-address-autocomplete, smartplay-hk-oss and wat-wat-new-zealand; the folder decides project identity and visibility, parseProjectDocument rejects unknown folders and disagreeing Visibility lines, and every chunk prefix states the project. Adding a project is a four-file change kept in lockstep with PROJECT_LABELS, PRIVATE_PROJECT_LABELS and the DB CHECK list.

nodes.label: Services-document offering chunk prefix
nodes.rationale: src/data/services/<offering>/*.md splits into packages/ (new builds) and support/ (Go Support Plan); the folder is the only source of truth for the offering, parseServicesDocument rejects an unknown folder, and the offering label is the first line of the prefix repeated on every chunk. sourceId stays the bare file name so adding the split needed no stale-row purge.

nodes.label: Untrusted evidence block
nodes.rationale: prompt-evidence wraps chunk text in <untrusted_evidence> with angle brackets and ampersands escaped and content JSON-quoted; chunk text is data, never instructions.

nodes.label: upsertSourceChunks as unit of truth
nodes.rationale: Replaces all chunks for a (source_type, source_id) inside one transaction and deletes stale indices; not-found/unpublished/empty content means removeSource rather than an error or zero-chunk write.

nodes.label: MODERATION_MIN_CONFIDENCE 0.6 gate
nodes.rationale: Lowered from 0.75 on 2026-10-02 after binary contact-question rewrites made hostile categories score 0.99-1.0 while real enquiries were being rejected at 0.69-0.71; it gates every safety and contact-intent decision, so lowering it is a blunt global instrument and criterion wording should be fixed first. Scope confidence is deliberately not gated on chat.

nodes.label: Direct /contact vs chat contact workflow
nodes.rationale: Two deliberately different screening paths (markers direct_contact_page vs fresh_contact_only; intent+safety vs safety+template_fit/template_choice) that must not be unified: template fit is meaningless on a template-less page, and checkContact judges intent before safety so spam is never described to the safety model and no category leaks to the submitter.

nodes.label: Label sets are contracts
nodes.rationale: Criteria-map keys are the only labels the decider may return and requiredAnswer throws otherwise (surfacing as 503, never a wrong-category error); accepted lists must be derived from map keys rather than hand-maintained parallel arrays, because the chat contact workflow's duplicated arrays are where drift happens.

nodes.label: Decision prompt budget (13,000 chars)
nodes.rationale: tests/server/decision-classifier.test.ts pins JSON.stringify(requestBody.questions).length < 13_000 on the chat-and-tools path (raised from 12,000 when production moved to the 256K-context v1.2); the budget must be logged inside the test because the documented measurement command stubs question text and undercounts.

nodes.label: Scope: asking vs producing
nodes.rationale: technical_question covers understanding, comparison, advice or a recommendation (interview-style), not production: write/generate/refactor/debug, role-play, or perform an action is general_knowledge, as is a follow-up that only adds detail to such a request (follow-up rule) or a bare fragmented mention (bare-mention rule).
